title: 2 Turno — Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro
description: Compare your positions with the proposals of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Similarity of answers is not a voting recommendation.

questions.text: The government should offer low-interest credit to develop industrial sectors it identifies as strategic.
Which economic sectors grow should be decided by the choices of businesses and consumers, not by government priorities.
Government purchases should favour products made in Brazil, even if they cost more.
Fuel price adjustments should pass on international market fluctuations directly, including when prices rise.
The government should set production and innovation goals to guide investment in strategic sectors.
The government should reduce the requirements for starting and running a business, while keeping product safety rules.
Benefits for low-income families should grow faster than inflation when public revenue permits.
Spending on social benefits should grow more slowly than public revenue to reduce public debt.
Income-transfer benefits should continue for as long as a family remains in poverty.
When a family finds employment, income-transfer benefits should end gradually over a transition period.
The government should enrol in social programmes the families who are entitled to benefits but do not yet receive them.
When budget resources are insufficient, social benefit rules should be reviewed to align spending with available resources.
Income-tax cuts for lower earners should be funded by higher taxes on very high incomes.
Tax policy should prioritize reducing the overall tax burden over redistributing taxation between income groups.
Profits and dividends received by very high earners should contribute to a minimum income tax.
Cutting taxes on consumption should take priority over raising taxes on the highest incomes.
The government should close tax breaks used mainly by high earners, even if this increases their tax bill.
Cutting business taxes should take priority over increasing taxation of the highest incomes.
To expand healthcare access, the government should prioritise expanding the public SUS network.
To shorten SUS waiting lists, the government should prioritise purchasing available capacity in private hospitals.
State-owned enterprises in strategic sectors should remain under public control.
Where public school places are unavailable, the government should fund places in private schools or childcare centres.
Expansion of higher education should prioritise new places at public universities and institutes.
Infrastructure expansion should prioritise concessions operated by private companies.
The law should shorten the working week and guarantee two rest days without reducing wages.
Workers and employers should have more freedom to negotiate working hours while respecting basic constitutional rights.
A national rule should give the minimum wage real increases beyond inflation.
There should be contracts with different rules from the standard labour code (CLT) to make it easier to hire young people and people over 50.
The government should inspect independent-contractor arrangements to prevent them replacing jobs that should have labour-code protections.
App drivers and couriers should remain self-employed, with their own social protection instead of standard employment contracts (CLT).
The government should maintain programmes and agencies specifically for LGBT people.
Abortion should remain allowed only in the cases already set out in law.
Racial quotas for access to education should be kept.
Eligibility for female sporting categories should be determined by sex at birth.
Public policy should recognise different family structures, including same-sex couples.
Parents or guardians should give prior permission for their children to attend lessons on sexuality.
Laws should be justified by public reasons accessible to people of different beliefs, without depending on a specific religious doctrine.
Religious values should have an explicit role in defining government priorities.
The government should apply the same criteria to different religions and to people without a religion.
Commitment to religious values should be one of the criteria when choosing officials such as ministers and higher-court judges.
Access to public services should be guaranteed regardless of participation in religious practices.
Public schools should be able to offer instruction in a specific religious tradition when requested by families.
Civilian firearm purchases should require proof of need as well as background and competency checks.
Firearm-carrying rights should extend to professional groups exposed to risk, such as lawyers.
There should be low limits on how many firearms and how much ammunition each civilian can buy.
Rules for collectors, sport shooters and hunters should make legally registered firearms easier to purchase and transport.
A federal civilian authority should centralise oversight of civilian firearms.
Adults who pass background and competency checks should have broader access to firearms for personal defence.
Prisons should offer more places for study and work to people serving sentences.
The age of adult criminal responsibility should fall from 18 to 16.
Progression to less restrictive prison regimes should remain possible for people convicted of heinous crimes who meet the legal criteria.
Prison policy should prioritise building new prisons, so that more convicts serve their sentences in closed custody.
Non-custodial sentences should be expanded for non-violent offences.
Police forces should have greater operational autonomy in decisions on the use of force, with less detailed federal rules.
High-impact projects should undergo full environmental studies even if licensing takes longer.
Environmental licensing should have shorter deadlines to accelerate productive projects.
Emissions-reduction targets should guide investment and land-use decisions.
Brazil should expand oil and gas exploration in new areas subject to environmental requirements.
The government should seek net-zero deforestation, including compensation for legally permitted clearing.
Income generation from natural resources should take priority where extraction can meet environmental law.
Brazil should pursue solutions to international conflicts through institutions such as the UN.
Foreign policy should prioritise direct agreements between countries over commitments to large blocs.
Brazil should deepen political and economic integration with South American countries.
Brazil should have greater freedom to negotiate trade agreements outside Mercosur's common rules.
Brazil should participate in international coalitions on hunger and climate change.
Brazil should preserve its autonomy by avoiding international commitments that limit decisions on its domestic policies.
Courts should be able to suspend unconstitutional actions by elected branches even when those actions have popular support.
The Supreme Court should focus on constitutional questions, leaving other kinds of cases to the rest of the judiciary.
A Supreme Court justice should be able to suspend a measure urgently if the full court reviews it promptly.
In public-policy disputes, courts should leave greater discretion to Congress and the executive.
Oversight bodies should be able to investigate government decisions without prior permission from elected officials.
The right to challenge laws directly before the Supreme Court should be limited to a smaller group of institutions.

proposals.text: The federal government should support expanding public schools following the civic-military model.
Brazil should seek to become a member of the OECD.
An environmental licence should be granted if the applicant meets the legal requirements and the environmental authority neither decides nor responds within the deadline.
Criminal factions should be officially classified as terrorist organisations.
The installation of data centres in Brazil should include local content requirements.
The government should expand the regulation of social media and digital platforms.
The government should continue settling encamped families through land reform.
The federal government should expand incentives for police forces to use body cameras.
